articles.author: Mandeep Singh
articles.description: Somatic mutations are increasingly implicated in persistent intestinal inflammation in chronic enteropathies. This review examines how mutation-bearing immune and epithelial clones may emerge, expand and contribute to disease within the chronically inflamed gut. We focus on refractory coeliac disease, highlighting the recent evidence for lymphoma-associated mutations in expanded intraepithelial lymphocyte clones in both type I and type II disease. We then consider emerging evidence in other...
articles.title: Somatic mutations in coeliac disease and other enteropathies: From chronic inflammation to clonal immune disease

articles.author: Giuseppe Mirabile
articles.description: CONCLUSION: This case represents a suspected donor-derived myeloid neoplasm arising after allo-HSCT and illustrates the diagnostic difficulty of distinguishing donor-derived disease from relapse and other post-transplant myeloid neoplasms. The case also highlights the potential value of integrating serial flow cytometry, molecular profiling, and lineage-specific chimerism analyses when unexplained cytopenias or progressive abnormal myeloid populations develop despite preserved donor chimerism....
articles.title: Suspected Donor-derived Myeloid Neoplasia After Allogeneic HSCT: A Case-based Review of Clonal Evolution

articles.author: Davide Santagata
articles.description: Inflammation and coagulation are tightly interconnected host-defense systems that, when dysregulated, promote pathological thrombosis. This narrative review examines mechanisms, clinical settings, and therapeutic implications of thromboinflammation (TI) across venous, arterial, and microvascular thrombosis, with particular attention to the differences in clinical translation among vascular territories. Endothelial activation, tissue factor expression, platelet-leukocyte interactions, neutrophil...
articles.title: Inflammation and thrombosis: from pathophysiology to future treatments

articles.author: Quanneng Zhao
articles.description: Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is a heterogeneous and rapidly changing biological pool derived from malignant cells, normal tissues, and hematopoietic cells. The abundance and molecular composition of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) are determined not only by tumor burden but also by tissue architecture, vascular access, cell-death programs, chromatin organization, nuclease processing, systemic clearance, treatment exposure, and clonal evolution. These biological determinants shape the mutation,...
articles.title: Cellular origins and evolutionary dynamics of plasma cfDNA in solid tumors: integrating germline, tumor-derived, and hematopoietic variation for MRD and treatment guidance

articles.author: Hironori Harada
articles.description: Myelodysplastic syndromes/neoplasms (MDS) are clonal myeloid malignancies arising from hematopoietic stem cell abnormalities. Treatment is risk-adapted: in lower-risk MDS, the primary goals are hematologic improvement and reduction of progression risk, and agents such as lenalidomide, erythropoiesis-stimulating agents, and luspatercept are commonly used. In contrast, higher-risk MDS requires disease-modifying approaches aimed at preventing leukemic transformation and prolonging survival, with...
articles.title: Advances in the management of myelodysplastic neoplasms

articles.author: Masayuki Yamashita
articles.description: Myeloid neoplasia comprises a spectrum of disorders now recognized as a continuum, ranging from clonal hematopoiesis to overt disease. Recent genomic studies have shown that hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) harboring somatic mutations undergo clonal expansion long before clinical manifestation. Although these mutant stem cells often retain multilineage differentiation potential, their intrinsic functions-including self-renewal capacity and differentiation dynamics-are altered. In addition,...
articles.title: Dysregulated control of hematopoietic stem cells in myeloid malignancies

articles.author: Soichi Sano
articles.description: Somatic mosaicism is emerging as a fundamental feature of human aging. Among its most common manifestations in men is acquired loss of the Y chromosome (LOY) in the hematopoietic system, which is most readily detected in blood cells. Although this has long been regarded as a largely incidental consequence of aging, the view is now changing. Epidemiologic studies, human genetic analyses, and experimental models have linked LOY to clonal hematopoiesis, immune dysregulation, chronic inflammation,...
articles.title: Y chromosome loss in hematopoietic cells and its clinical implications

articles.description: A somatic mutation causing clonal expansion in hematopoietic stem cells (HSC), but not resulting in hematologic malignancy, is termed clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP). Because osteoclasts are derived from the macrophage-monocyte lineage of HSCs, changes in the bone marrow niche due to CHIP may drive changes in...

articles.description: Accelerated atherosclerosis (AA) denotes a disproportionately early and rapid progression of arterial atheroma unpredictable by standard tools. Clinicians often rely on simplified frameworks for cardiovascular risk assessment, which may overlook genetic and pathological conditions associated with AA. Some of these are well established, others are considered future therapy targets. This review examines the conditions in which AA is most firmly established, including rheumatoid arthritis (RA),...

articles.author: Abdullah M AlShahrani
articles.description: CONCLUSION: Current evidence supports a spectrum of mechanisms ranging from selection of pre-existing clones to therapy-induced de novo mutation. Existing literature cannot support universal CH screening recommendations or guide treatment decisions. Prospective serial analyses harmonized on definition, employing sensitive baseline assays with paired germline controls and tumor-contamination checks, are needed to justify clinical implementation and assessment of fixed outcomes.
articles.title: Clonal Hematopoiesis Across the Cancer Treatment Continuum: A Scoping Review of Clonal Selection, Evolution, and Clinical Outcomes

articles.author: Sumedha Agashe
articles.description: Somatic mutations in the de novo methyltransferase DNMT3A and cytosine demethylase TET2 are common in age-related clonal hematopoiesis and hematopoietic neoplasms. TET2 mutations, unlike DNMT3A mutations, increase sensitivity to PARP inhibitors (PARPi). We find that TET2 loss, but not DNMT3A loss, alters DNA replication fork progression upon treatment with PARPi Olaparib, resulting in longer DNA replication tracts and increased DNA breaks. This reveals a new link between abnormal fork elongation...
articles.title: TET2 loss triggers ssDNA gap accumulation and heightened PARP inhibitor sensitivity

We tested whether somatic mutations in the blood were associated with incident frailty and faster progression in 730,088 participants from UK Biobank, All of Us, BioVU and the Women's Health Initiative. We found that clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) and autosomal mosaic chromosomal alterations...
articles.title: Clonal Hematopoiesis Accelerates Frailty and Functional Decline

articles.author: Aeron M Small
articles.description: CONCLUSIONS: Integrating human cohort data with experimental evidence using ASXL1 -mutant human macrophage-like cells and human valve cells, these findings identify ASXL1 -mutant CHIP as a distinct inflammatory subtype associated with valvular calcification and support IL-1 and IL-6 signaling as candidate therapeutic pathways for future investigation in CAVD.
articles.title: ASXL1- Mutant Clonal Hematopoiesis is Associated with Calcific Aortic Valve Disease and Promotes Valvular Calcification In Vitro

articles.author: Isaac F López-Moyado

articles.author: Yuhang Li
articles.description: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) is an early indicator of hematologic malignancies, driven by mutations in hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) such as TET2 or P53. Recently ZBTB33 mutations have been implicated in myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) and suggested as a driver of CH. However, the role of ZBTB33 in hematopoiesis and its causative involvement in CH remains unclear. We generated a Zbtb33-knockout mouse strain to elucidate its function in hematopoiesis and tumor growth. Our findings indicate that...
articles.title: Loss of transcriptional factor Zbtb33 fails to induce clonal hematopoiesis in mice but plays a role in tumor growth

articles.description: The bispecific CD19/CD3 T-cell engaging antibody blinatumomab is efficacious in front-line therapy in B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) but the biological determinants of response and resistance are incompletely understood. In a recent study published in Nature Cell Biology, Mistry and colleagues uncover that senescence in the bone marrow stromal microenvironment is a key contributor to the clonal growth of haematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) carrying CH mutations. Using mouse models...
articles.title: Getting comfortable: clonal haematopoiesis creates a senescent niche for expansion

articles.author: Rie Nishi
articles.description: Myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) are a group of clonal myeloid neoplasms characterized by ineffective hematopoiesis and cytopenia. Hypomethylating agents (HMAs) serve a central role in the treatment of high-risk MDS, but their mechanisms of action are diverse and not fully understood. To investigate the molecular mechanisms of HMAs, an MDS cell line (MDS-L) was cultured with a non-toxic concentration of decitabine (DAC) for 6 months and drug sensitivity, cell differentiation and DNA methylation...
articles.title: Decitabine induces cell differentiation and growth inhibition accompanied by upregulation of microRNA-143 and MS4A3 in the myelodysplastic syndromes-derived leukemic cell line MDS-L

When clonal expansions occur in the blood system, they are referred to as 'clonal haematopoiesis' or 'clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate...

articles.author: Jana H Husein
articles.description: CONCLUSION: This systematic review identifies that malignant progression is dictated by a qualitative proteomic "switch" and structural niche reorganization. However, causal relationships remain to be definitively established. We identify a critical "Spatial Architecture Gap" in current research, highlighting the need for spatial proteomic platforms to map the physical "handshake" between mutant clones and their inflammatory environment to enable early clinical interception.
articles.title: The proteomic architecture of clonal hematopoiesis: a systematic review of niche remodeling and multi-compartment predictors of malignant transformation

articles.description: Haematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) are important for human health and clinical therapy. Aging is associated with a decline in the function of the HSC pool and haematopoietic perturbations. Additionally, aging correlates with clonal haematopoiesis, driven by the accumulation of genetic mutations in this long-lived cell population that can lead to altered cell function and...

Here, we identify lysophosphatidylcholine acyltransferase 3 (LPCAT3), a key enzyme of the Lands' cycle, as a critical...
articles.title: LPCAT3 is essential for leukemia progression and represents a therapeutic vulnerability in AML

articles.author: Melissa V Bergman
articles.description: CONCLUSION: The prevalence of ASXL1 exon 12 variants in our AML cohort was consistent with international data. Variants in the elderly population were very prevalent; however, with no actionable variants capable of driving clonal expansion, clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential was not detected. The variants of uncertain significance at allele frequencies of ≥ 2% likely suggest a clonal haematopoietic process.
articles.title: Additional sex combs-like 1 variants in an acute myeloid leukaemia and a general elderly cohort in central South Africa

Emerging evidence suggests that alterations in cellular homeostasis shape cancer progression. However, the mechanisms underlying AML progression remain largely unclear. Here, we identify lysophosphatidylcholine acyltransferase 3 (LPCAT3), a key enzyme of the Lands' cycle, as a critical...
articles.title: LPCAT3 is essential for leukemia progression and represents a therapeutic vulnerability in AML

articles.author: Melissa V Bergman
articles.description: CONCLUSION: The prevalence of ASXL1 exon 12 variants in our AML cohort was consistent with international data. Variants in the elderly population were very prevalent; however, with no actionable variants capable of driving clonal expansion, clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential was not detected. The variants of uncertain significance at allele frequencies of ≥ 2% likely suggest a clonal haematopoietic process.
articles.title: Additional sex combs-like 1 variants in an acute myeloid leukaemia and a general elderly cohort in central South Africa

Here, we demonstrate that pairing a near-telomere-to-telomere (near-T2T) diploid assembly of a donor with deep short- and long-read sequencing of their melanoma reveals that 16% of somatic variants localize to sequences absent from GRCh38, with satellite repeats acting as hotspots for UV-associated mutagenesis. articles.description: Therapy-related myeloid neoplasms (t-MNs), which develop following cytotoxic chemotherapy or radiotherapy, remain one of the most significant clinical challenges in modern hematology due to their aggressive clinical course and poor survival outcomes. articles.author: Atri Choksi
articles.description: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), obtained serially during cancer treatment, can capture tumor burden trends to help interpret response and detect resistance to systemic therapy for patients with advanced disease. Traditionally, tumor-informed assays track somatic variants identified from an initial tumor biopsy and have demonstrated prognostic utility for early-stage disease. However, tumor-informed ctDNA assays are potentially limited by logistical and methodologic considerations in the setting...
articles.title: Concordance of tumor-informed and tumor-agnostic ctDNA assays for treatment response monitoring in advanced solid tumors

articles.author: Resham Mawalkar
articles.description: Calreticulin gene (CALR) mutations are seen in 25%-30% of myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs). We report outcomes and high-risk genomic signatures in 149 patients with CALR-mutated MPN. CALR-mutated essential thrombocythaemia (n = 106) progressed to myelofibrosis (n = 40) at a median of 20.4 years, and 20-year overall survival (OS) was 81%. In 83 patients with myelofibrosis, the median leukaemia-free survival (LFS) was 12.9 years, and OS was 13.9 years. Median survival after leukaemia...
articles.title: Outcome heterogeneity in CALR-mutated myeloproliferative neoplasms

In this Primer, we consider how different mouse-modeling strategies can be aligned with human tumor evolution, focusing on mutation order, the emergence and competition of initially rare mutant clones within genetically mosaic tissues, and microenvironmental context. By...

Perturbation of tumorigenesis by experimental alteration of oncogenes and tumor suppressors in genetically engineered mouse models has long served to inform human cancer research and such...
articles.title: Cancer evolution in its native host: oncogenic selection and epistasis revealed by human tumor genomes

articles.author: Qi Zhang
articles.description: Mosaic loss of the Y chromosome (mLOY) is a male‑specific somatic loss of the Y chromosome that is predominantly observed in peripheral blood leukocytes, but can also be found in other tissue types. It represents one of the most common male-specific somatic mutations, particularly prevalent in aging individuals. Accumulating evidence shows that mLOY markedly increases the incidence, progression, and adverse prognosis of multiple diseases, including, but not limited to, myocardial fibrosis, lung...

articles.author: Roni Haas
articles.description: Multifocal prostate cancer is a prevalent phenomenon, with most cases remaining uncharacterized from a genomic perspective. A patient presented with bilateral prostate cancer. On systematic biopsy, two indistinguishable clinicopathologic lesions were detected. Whole-genome sequencing displayed somatically unrelated tumors with distinct driver CNA regions, suggesting independent origins of the two tumors. We demonstrated that similar clinicopathologic multifocal tumors, which might be interpreted...
articles.title: Divergent evolution in bilateral prostate cancer: a case study

articles.author: Xuyu Chen
articles.description: Early gastric cancer is still commonly conceptualized as the endpoint of a linear sequence from chronic gastritis to intestinal metaplasia, dysplasia, and invasion. Yet recent single-cell, spatial, genomic, and functional studies indicate that this model incompletely captures the biology of early gastric carcinogenesis. Malignant potential is established progressively within a precancerous gastric field already shaped by somatic evolution, chronic inflammatory injury, and epithelial lineage...
articles.title: Reframing early gastric carcinogenesis through lineage, niche, and evolution

articles.description: Early gastric cancer is still commonly conceptualized as the endpoint of a linear sequence from chronic gastritis to intestinal metaplasia, dysplasia, and invasion. Yet recent single-cell, spatial, genomic, and functional studies indicate that this model incompletely captures the biology of early gastric carcinogenesis. Malignant potential is established progressively within a precancerous gastric field already shaped by somatic evolution, chronic inflammatory injury, and epithelial lineage...
articles.title: Reframing early gastric carcinogenesis through lineage, niche, and evolution

articles.description: Genetic heterogeneity and clonal outgrowths are observed even in otherwise healthy human tissues, shaping the genetic composition of cell populations in non-malignant disease and during physiological ageing. This clonal mosaicism likely provides the pre-cancerous seeds for malignant transformation. Once a tumour arises, clonal evolution poses a major challenge to achieving cure, as clonal diversification provides an expanded number of substrates upon which therapy can act as a selective...

articles.author: Nicole Heinzl
articles.description: High grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSC) has low survival partly due to the lack of methods for detection, diagnosis, and risk prediction. TP53 mutations, which drive HGSC, are found in gynecological tissues as the result of somatic evolution, but it is unknown whether an excess of mutations is linked to ovarian cancer. Here we investigate if TP53 mutation burden measured in uterine lavage, a minimally invasive gynecological liquid biopsy, can discriminate between patients with and without HGSC....
articles.title: High-grade serous ovarian cancer is associated with increased TP53 mutation burden in uterine lavage

articles.author: Qianqian Chen
articles.description: Malignant tumors have long been viewed as uncontrolled cell proliferation driven by somatic mutations. However, emerging multi-omics and microenvironment evidence challenges this paradigm. Advanced tumors transcend cellular abnormality to form a "neoorgan" - a complex tissue ecosystem with multicellular coordination, functional autonomy, metabolic symbiosis, neural integration, and evolutionary potential. Genomic instability generates lineage-specific karyotypes; tumors reactivate ancient gene...
articles.title: Evolution of malignant tumors as neoorgan and predictions of future scenarios resulting from inappropriate treatment

Advanced tumors transcend cellular abnormality to form a "neoorgan" - a complex tissue ecosystem with multicellular coordination, functional autonomy, metabolic symbiosis, neural integration, and evolutionary potential. Genomic instability generates lineage-specific karyotypes; tumors reactivate ancient gene...
articles.title: Evolution of malignant tumors as neoorgan and predictions of future scenarios resulting from inappropriate treatment
